extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, appellants, respondents, and administrative patent judges participating in appeals, reexaminations, contested cases, and inter partes proceedings before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules of practice and procedural requirements for appeals, rehearings, oral hearings, briefs, evidence, motions, discovery, contested cases, and patent interferences before the USPTO Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of supplemental examiner's answer / new issues in reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may file a supplemental examiner's answer unless the reply brief raises new issues; examples of new issues include arguing nonanalogous art or different claim limitations in a reply brief that were not raised in the principal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) Brief argues that element 4 of reference B cannot be combined with A; reply brief argues B is nonanalogous art (new issue). (2) Brief argues pump means not taught; reply argues retaining means not taught (new issue). An appellant who disagrees with an examiner's decision that a supplemental examiner's answer is permitted may petition under Rule 181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection and reopening prosecution requires supervisory approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may withdraw a final rejection and reopen prosecution as an alternative to issuing a supplemental examiner's answer, but such a decision requires approval from the supervisory patent examiner as set forth in MPEP 1208.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and extension for supplemental reply briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may file a supplemental reply brief in response to a supplemental examiner's answer within two months from the date of the supplemental examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period may be extended under Rule 136(b) for patent applications and Rule 550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings as set forth in § 41.43(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for oral hearing caption and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate paper requesting the oral hearing must be captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' and can be filed within two months from the date of the examiner's answer or supplemental examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where § 41.47(b) requires the separate captioned paper; similar requirement appears in § 41.73(b) for other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on evidence and arguments at oral hearing; order of argument
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing appellant may only rely on evidence previously considered by the primary examiner and present argument relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except as permitted by paragraph (e)(2); the primary examiner is similarly limited to arguments/evidence raised in the answer or supplemental answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order of argument: appellant opens, then the primary examiner argues, then appellant concludes (appellant opens and concludes; appellant should reserve some time for concluding argument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause for new arguments at hearing based on recent decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a showing of good cause, appellant and/or the primary examiner may rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exception to the general limitation on new arguments at oral hearing and rehearing (see § 41.47(e)(2), § 41.52(a)(2), § 41.73(e)(2), § 41.79(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to deny oral hearing in certain situations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may decide no hearing is necessary where, prior to hearing, it is convinced the application must be remanded for further consideration or that the examiner's position cannot be sustained in any event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to conserve resources where a hearing would be futile or preliminary remand is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of periods under Rule 136(b) and Rule 550(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods set forth in the sections governing appeals, hearings, and replies are extendable under the provisions of Rule 136(b) for patent applications and Rule 550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extension provision appeared in former rules (e.g., former Rule 191(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Board decision: affirm, reverse, remand
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, in reviewing adverse examiner decisions, may affirm or reverse the decision of the examiner in whole or in part on the grounds and claims specified by the examiner; affirmance of a rejection on any grounds specified constitutes general affirmance of the examiner's decision on that claim except as to reversed grounds, and the Board may remand an application to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond to supplemental examiner's answer after remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must respond to any supplemental examiner's answer issued in response to a Board remand to avoid sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must either (i) request prosecution be reopened before the examiner by filing a reply under Rule 111 with or without amendment or evidence (Rules 130–132), which is treated as a request to withdraw the appeal; or (ii) request the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief as provided in § 41.41. If a reply brief is accompanied by any amendment/affidavit/evidence it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution (withdraw appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may suggest amendments and appellant's right to amend in conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's opinion may include an explicit statement how a claim could be amended to overcome a specific rejection; when the Board includes such a statement appellant has the right to amend in conformity therewith, which would overcome that specific rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may still reject a claim so-amended if the rejection constitutes a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely respond to Board order may result in dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant's failure to timely respond to an order of the Board could result in dismissal of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and exceptions on rehearing arguments and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised in the briefs before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon in the briefs are not permitted in the request for rehearing, except as permitted upon a showing of good cause or when responding to a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.52(a)(1)–(3) and § 41.79(b)(2)–(3) for specific allowances: new arguments based on recent Board or Federal Court decisions allowed for good cause; new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and filing certificate requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Key terms for subpart C proceedings: 'proceeding' shorthand for inter partes reexamination proceeding; 'owner', 'requester', 'appellant', 'respondent' defined; 'filing' requires any document filed to include a certificate indicating service to all other parties as required by Rule 903.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one party appeals or cross-appeals, each is an appellant with respect to the claims directed by their appeal; no requester may be a respondent to another requester's appellant brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on post-appeal amendments and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted after the date the proceeding has been appealed are prohibited except for amendments permitted by § 41.77(b)(1) and amendments canceling claims where such cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim. Affidavits and other evidence submitted after appeal are likewise prohibited except as permitted by § 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces prior practice permitting such evidence on a showing of good and sufficient reasons; the Office expects prosecution to occur before the examiner prior to an appeal being filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment of jurisdiction to examining operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over a proceeding may be relinquished and the proceeding returned to the examining operation to permit processing to be completed before the Board takes up the appeal for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief copy requirements (one copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of the brief is required rather than three, consistent with the Office's move to an electronic file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify real party in interest in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement in the brief is required identifying by name the real party in interest even if the party named in the caption of the brief is the real party in interest, to comply with § 41.8(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify related prior and pending proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs must clearly identify all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, or judicial proceedings known to appellant, the appellant's legal representative, or assignee that may be related to, directly affect, or have a bearing on the Board's decision in the pending appeal, to comply with § 41.8(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: State status of all claims and identify appealed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief must include a statement of the status of all the claims in the proceeding (e.g., rejected, allowed, confirmed, withdrawn, objected to, canceled) and identify those claims that are being appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation of subject matter of independent claims with specification and drawing references
rubrics_metrics.description: For each independent claim involved in the appeal and each dependent claim argued separately, a concise explanation of the subject matter defined in the claim is required and shall refer to the specification by page and line number and to the drawings, if any, by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each independent claim and each dependent claim argued separately, every means-plus-function and step-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph) must be identified and the structure, material, or acts described in the specification as corresponding to each claimed function be set forth with reference to the specification by page and line number and to the drawing by reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise statement listing each issue presented for review
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement is required listing each issue presented for review (example: 'claims 1 to 10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. X').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is § 41.67(c)(1)(vi) and intended to provide clear, compact presentation of issues for the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of claims and waiver for failure to argue separately
rubrics_metrics.description: The former grouping requirement is removed, but when an appellant argues multiple claims as a group under the same ground of rejection the Board may select a single claim to decide; failure to argue separately claims that appellant has grouped together constitutes a waiver of any separate argument regarding the patentability of grouped claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims argued separately should be placed under a subheading identifying the claim by number; grouped claims should be under a subheading identifying the claims by number. See In re McDaniel for interpretation of former analogous rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments must show why claims are separately patentable (not just differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Merely pointing out differences in what the claims cover is not an argument as to why the claims are separately patentable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants must do more than identify differences; must explain why those differences render claims patentable over applied art or grounds of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to consider arguments or authorities not included in brief without good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any arguments or authorities not included in a brief permitted in the section or filed pursuant to §§ 41.68 and 41.71 will be refused consideration by the Board unless good cause is shown; a separate heading is required for each ground of rejection instead of prior grouping of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces clear organization and completeness in briefs; good cause exceptions exist but are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix requirement in appellant's brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must include an evidence appendix of any evidence relied upon in the appeal with a statement setting forth where that evidence was entered in the record by the examiner so the Board can reference such evidence easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.67(c)(1)(ix). This facilitates Board review by locating evidence quickly in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must include a related proceedings appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified pursuant to § 41.67(c)(1)(ii) so the Board can consider such decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence from briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence is excluded from being included in an appellant's brief (and likewise a respondent's brief) except as expressly permitted by the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.67(c)(2) and § 41.68(b)(2) — evidence not previously admitted is excluded to preserve record integrity and preclude late submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent briefs: prohibition on new/non-admitted evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.68 generally incorporates former Rule 967 and explicitly excludes any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence from a respondent's brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers filing standards and acceptable paper formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to be filed must meet standards similar to those required in patent prosecution (Rule 52(a)) and Fed. R. App. P. 32; a party may file papers in either A4 or 8.5"×11" format but may not alternate between formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board presently prefers 8.5"×11" because the filing system is best adapted to that format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet and paper formatting requirements (holes, no incorporation by reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover sheet format of a paper is codified; holes at the top of the paper consistent with Local Civil Rule 5.1(f) are required to facilitate entry in the administrative record; incorporation by reference and combination of papers is barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar against incorporation/combination minimizes chance an argument will be overlooked and reduces abuses from incorporations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working copy filing requirement for Board official
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of a working copy for the Board official administering the proceeding is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.106(c). This ensures the panel has an easily usable copy when considering papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special modes of filing guidance (mail, express mail, other modes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for special modes of filing encourages use of USPS EXPRESS MAIL®; other modes of filing are permitted under § 41.106(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged modes aim to ensure timely physical delivery where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers when filed and expedited service
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be served when they are filed if they have not already been served; expedited service procedures are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of service must be incorporated into each paper other than exhibits; when exhibits are filed at the same time the certificate may be incorporated into the exhibit list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of counsel and lead counsel requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must identify its counsel, if any; the Board may require appointment of a lead counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows § 41.108 and analogous former Rule 613(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to obtain copies of Office files and duty to notify Board if not received
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may obtain copies of certain Office files directly related to the contested case. A party that has not received copies of a requested file must promptly notify the Board of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single clean set of claims requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A single clean set of the claims is required, analogous to 'clean form' amendments under Rule 121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of requested relief and basis in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Contested cases require notice of requested relief and the basis for that relief to be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions practice focused on the central issue of contested case
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions practice is redefined to focus more specifically on the central issue in the contested case; motions may include motion for judgment in the contest, attacking standing or seeking relief on the central issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications include responsive and miscellaneous motion practice to ensure the proceeding remains focused; miscellaneous motions permit requests for relief on procedural or tangential issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on moving party
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.121(b) places the burden of proof on the moving party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows Rule 637(a) (2003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions formatting and content requirements; separate paper per motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions must follow content rules (short numbered paragraphs stating material facts, ideally one or two sentences each) and a separate paper is required for each motion; sloppy drafting is held against the moving party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A movant must make showings ordinarily required for the requested relief in other parts of the Office; see § 41.121(c)(1)–(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to raise patentability questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is allowed to raise questions of patentability sua sponte during contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codified practice regarding new arguments in replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.122 codifies the present practice regarding new arguments in replies (i.e., limits and treatment of new arguments raised in reply briefs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Default times for filing motions and miscellaneous motion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.123 sets default times for filing motions and provides requirements for miscellaneous motions to keep proceedings on schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument requests and procedures for contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request oral argument, but requests are not automatically granted; three working copies of papers required for panel hearings; default time is 20 minutes per party for oral arguments at the Board; demonstrative exhibits permitted; transcription of argument permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.124(a)–(e). Oral hearings are not evidentiary hearings and time limits are set accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision short of judgment not final and rehearing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision short of judgment is not final; the rule recodifies the time for requesting rehearing and procedural requirements for rehearing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recodified arbitration practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.126 recodifies the Office's existing arbitration practice for appropriate matters in Board proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel, final disposal, concession inference, and rehearing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.127 recodifies estoppel provisions for interferences, restates final disposal provisions, outlines conditions under which the Board may infer concession of the contest, restates recommendation provision, and provides a time for requesting rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: misleading arguments, dilatory tactics, and terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.128 restates Rule 616 on sanctions and adds misleading arguments and dilatory tactics to the list of reasons for sanctions; available sanctions include those in Rule 616 and may add terminal disclaimer requirement as a sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited discovery policy in contested proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy of limited discovery is restated to provide contested proceedings that are fast, inexpensive, and fair; automatic discovery of materials cited in an involved specification or benefit disclosure is provided; additional testimony governed by existing practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.150(a)–(c). The policy balances fairness and expedition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to comply with rules may challenge admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with the rules is a basis for challenging admissibility of evidence or submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.151 and Rule 671(i) practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Federal Rules of Evidence and official notice/hearsay for foreign law
rubrics_metrics.description: Contested cases continue the practice of using the Federal Rules of Evidence; § 41.152(d) permits reliance on official notice and hearsay to determine the scope and effect of foreign law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of Office records and exhibit submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Office records that are available to all parties may be admitted without certification; each Office record cited as evidence must be submitted as an exhibit; formal exhibit requirements (translation, formatting) are codified; an exhibit list is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §§ 41.153, 41.154(a)–(d), and § 41.154(b) on translation of foreign evidence (Rule 647).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objecting to evidence and responding to objections; timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Default time to serve an objection to evidence other than testimony is five business days; a party that submitted evidence ten business days after service of the objection may cure defects in the evidence; the Board ordinarily will not address an objection unless the objecting party files a motion to exclude; motion in limine permitted for ruling on admissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.155(b)–(d). Standing Order ¶ 14.2 provides two weeks in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for subpoenas and special requirements for foreign testimony/production
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking a subpoena must first obtain authorization from the Board; additional requirements are imposed for testimony or production outside the United States because foreign testimony increases cost and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony taking practices and cross-examination timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice regarding taking testimony is restated: time period for cross-examination is set in § 41.157(c)(2), documents provided in advance is limited to direct testimony, and a conference before a deposition with an interpreter is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct testimony is generally in the form of a declaration; advance document provision rarely applies except for compelled testimony. See § 41.157(c)(1)–(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer qualification, disqualification standard, transcript filing, and costs for testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'officer' (per 35 U.S.C. 23) is adopted for the person qualified to administer testimony; a standard for disqualifying an officer (substantially Rule 674) is adopted; the proponent of testimony must file the transcript; the proponent must pay reasonable costs associated with making the witness available for cross-examination (reporter, transcript).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on expert testimony and scientific tests/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.158 codifies existing practices regarding expert testimony and scientific tests and data for contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of patent interferences as contested cases and interpretation of copied claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent interferences are specifically identified as contested cases under subpart D; practice continues of looking at the applicant's specification (not the source specification) to determine the meaning of a copied claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum normal pendency for patent interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy sets two years as the maximum normal pendency for patent interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions specific to patent interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions include 'accorded benefit' (application providing proper constructive reduction to practice), 'constructive reduction to practice', 'count' redefined to emphasize relationship to admissible proofs of priority under § 102(g), 'involved claim' consistent with other definitions, 'senior party' focusing on earliest constructive reduction to practice, and 'threshold issue' defined to include no interference-in-fact, the bar under 35 U.S.C. 135(b), and lack of written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions clarify priority, standing, and which issues can bar participation in an interference; threshold issues are limited to motions from a party with a patent or published application against a party with an involved application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and practice for provoking an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants provoking an interference must follow requirements (adding a claim to provoke an interference, special requirements when copying claims from patents) and may be subject to summary proceedings if unable to show they would prevail on priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 41.202(d) provides bases for summary proceedings; showings under § 41.202(e) must by themselves, if unrebutted, warrant determination of priority in favor of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for declaring an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for declaring a patent interference is a two-way unpatentability test to determine whether claimed inventions interfere; an administrative patent judge declares the interference and may redeclare it sua sponte or in response to motions; parties may suggest that an APJ declare or redeclare an interference to accommodate files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of requested relief and simplification of priority statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of requested relief (priority statements) are simplified in formal requirements; parties are ordinarily limited to filing substantive motions consistent with their notice of requested relief. No default times set for statements in § 41.204(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing settlement agreements and termination of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of settlement agreements follows practice under Rule 666 and implements 35 U.S.C. 135(c); after a final decision by the Board, an interference is considered terminated when no appeal or other review has been or can be taken; if appeals/civil actions were filed the interference terminates when such proceedings are terminated (e.g., issuance of mandate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.205(a) and discussion referencing Rule 41(d)(2), Fed. R. App. P., and effects of certiorari stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice regarding commonly owned patents and real-party-in-interest control
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised practice addresses cases involving commonly owned patents and applications where a real party-in-interest has the ability to control conduct of more than one party in an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.206 for details addressing control and common ownership issues.
